subject.title: [Feature Request]: Native Prompt Caching Support for Amazon Nova (Bedrock)

question: Should OpenClaw intentionally change direct Amazon Bedrock Nova models from forced no-cache to native cache-point eligible behavior once live Nova proof is attached?
rationale: Current source proves the requested behavior is still missing, but enabling provider-side caching changes request shaping and runtime defaults for existing Nova users.

options.title: Land the linked provider fix after live proof
options.body: Require redacted Nova Converse or ConverseStream proof, refresh the branch, then accept the provider-owned policy change in the linked PR or a narrow replacement.

options.title: Require opt-in Nova caching
options.body: Preserve no-cache as the upgrade default and allow Nova cache points only through explicit configuration or a narrower policy gate.

options.title: Defer Nova native caching
options.body: Leave the current no-cache behavior in place until AWS docs, live proof, or provider ownership makes the default behavior less uncertain.

recommendation.title: Land the linked provider fix after live proof
recommendation.body: Require redacted Nova Converse or ConverseStream proof, refresh the branch, then accept the provider-owned policy change in the linked PR or a narrow replacement.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent Bedrock provider and release-history signals make this the strongest available routing candidate for the provider behavior decision.
